Review comments: Shrimp and grits were rich and perfectly cooked. Our server knew the menu well and made excellent wine suggestions. One of the best meals we had all year.
Soup dumplings were torn before they reached the table and the broth had leaked out. Staff seemed indifferent when we mentioned it. Would not return.
Standard pub menu. The burger was fine and the fries were crisp. Nothing stood out, but nothing was wrong either.
Wonderful mezze platter and the warmest service we have had in a long time. The baklava was flaky and not too sweet. Highly recommended.
Overpriced and underwhelming. The Valentine's prix fixe was rushed, the scallops were gritty, and we were asked to leave our table after 75 minutes.
Decent steak frites and a reasonable beer selection. The room was cold and service was slow, but the food made up for it somewhat.
The pad see ew was greasy and bland, and the spring rolls tasted reheated. Our order was also missing an entrée. Disappointing.
Fried flounder was light and crisp, hushpuppies were fresh from the fryer, and the view of the sound was beautiful. Worth the drive.
Crab cakes were mostly filler. Cocktails were good but expensive. An average experience overall.
Excellent carne asada tacos and a terrific house salsa. The patio is pleasant in the evening and the staff were quick and cheerful.
Waited over an hour for a table, then another 30 minutes for food. The pancakes were dense and the syrup was clearly not real maple. Not worth it.
Solid Southern menu. The fried chicken was good, the collards were too salty. Service was friendly but forgetful.
Superb veal saltimbocca and a thoughtful Italian wine list. The owner stopped by our table and was genuinely welcoming. A neighborhood gem.
Brisket was dry and the burnt ends were mostly fat. Sauce was too sweet. For a city known for barbecue, this was a letdown.
Interesting seasonal menu. The trout was nicely cooked but the vegetable sides were under-seasoned. Prices are on the high side for the portions.
Fresh, creative vegetarian dishes. The beet risotto was outstanding and the staff accommodated our allergies without any fuss.
The menu is enormous and the food is about what you would expect. General Tso's chicken was fine; the hot and sour soup was thin.
Lobster roll was small, mostly mayonnaise, and cost $38. The server was curt and the restroom was dirty. Avoid.
Blue corn enchiladas with red chile were excellent. Generous portions, low prices, and fast service. Everything we hoped for.
Classic French bistro dishes executed competently. The onion soup was good; the duck confit was slightly dry. Pleasant atmosphere.
Bagels were stale and the cream cheese was spread so thin it was barely there. The line was long and the staff were rude.
Dungeness crab was sweet and perfectly steamed. The garlic noodles were addictive. Service was relaxed and friendly. Will be back.
The ribeye was ordered medium-rare and arrived well done. A replacement took 25 minutes. The manager comped dessert, but the evening was ruined.
Afternoon tea service was pleasant. Scones were good, sandwiches were ordinary. A nice setting, if a little pricey for what you get.
Everything tasted like it had been picked that morning. The heirloom tomato salad and roast chicken were both excellent. Lovely, unhurried service.
Ramen broth was salty and lukewarm, and the chashu was tough. The music was so loud we could not hear each other. Not recommended.
Traditional menu with large portions. The pot roast was tender; the mashed potatoes came from a box. Fine for a family dinner.
Excellent pho with a deeply flavored broth and plenty of fresh herbs. The banh mi was also very good. Quick, friendly, and inexpensive.
Reservation was lost, we waited 45 minutes, and then the kitchen ran out of two dishes we wanted. The food we did get was mediocre.
Good bourbon list and a decent pork chop. The Brussels sprouts were burnt. Service was competent but impersonal.
Elk tenderloin was beautifully cooked and the room had a warm, cozy feel with the fireplace going. Staff were attentive and knowledgeable.
The menu tries to do too much. The sushi burrito was soggy and the truffle fries were cold. Prices are high for the quality.
Simple breakfast menu. Eggs and toast were fine, coffee was weak. Convenient location near the river trail.
Croissants were buttery and flaky, and the almond pastry was the best I have had in the U.S. Friendly staff and a charming space.
Burgers were overcooked and dry, the bun fell apart, and the milkshake machine was broken. Long wait for a disappointing meal.
Mesquite-grilled chicken was flavorful but the rice was undercooked. The patio heaters were welcome on a cool night. Mixed results.
Excellent fondue and a well-chosen wine list. The staff made our group of ten feel welcome and handled separate checks without complaint.
Pizza arrived burnt on the bottom and the toppings were sparse. Delivery was an hour late. We will order elsewhere next time.
Corned beef sandwich was respectable and the pickles were good. The soup of the day was forgettable. Reasonable prices.
Fried green tomatoes and hot chicken were both excellent. Live music in the background added to a great evening. Service was warm and quick.
The braised short rib was tender and well seasoned, though the portion was smaller than expected for the price. Service was attentive without hovering.
Excellent lamb tagine with a good balance of spice and sweetness. The dining room gets loud on weekends, so conversation was difficult.
Very fresh oysters and a solid clam chowder. We waited 40 minutes past our reservation time, which the staff acknowledged but did not otherwise address.
A quiet spot for brunch. The buckwheat pancakes were light and the coffee was strong. Limited seating, so arrive early.
Handmade pappardelle with wild boar ragù was the highlight. The tiramisu was overly sweet. Wine list is reasonably priced.
Wood-fired steaks cooked exactly to order. Sides were unremarkable, and the creamed spinach arrived lukewarm.
Rich tonkotsu broth and well-made noodles. Counter seating only, and the line moved slowly during lunch hour.
Seasonal tasting menu with strong local sourcing. Two of the seven courses felt underdeveloped, but the dessert course was outstanding.
Green chile enchiladas had real heat and depth. Margaritas were weak for the price. Friendly, efficient staff.
Reliable diner fare. The maple-glazed bacon and hash browns were good; the eggs were overcooked. Fast service and fair prices.
